summary: Closed the legibility gap T59-implementation.md disclosed for loadHealthConfig's present-but-unusable branch: the gate was already forced to its strictest reachable verdict (T59), but nothing in the returned GateResult said why. Added an additive HealthConfig.configUnreadable?:boolean flag (types.ts), mirroring SecurityConfig.configUnreadable exactly, set only in config.ts's existing unusable branch; computeGate (gate.ts) turns the flag into one constant, non-interpolated, leak-safe reason pushed onto reasons, the same way guard.ts turns configUnreadable into POSTURE_UNAVAILABLE_REASON. The push never calls escalate, so status/coverage are provably unchanged -- verified directly by a same-inputs/with-and-without-flag regression. Also resolved the residual T59 disclosed but did not fix: metrics.coverageSoftFloor is the one metrics field computeGate reads for a gate decision, so leaving it at the plain default (60) for an unusable config silently reverted an operator's tightened coverage-warn threshold exactly like the bug T59 closed for gate/sources; it is now forced to 100, the ceiling of its percentage range and therefore at least as strict as any real config. One pre-existing test assertion (metrics full-equality to default) was corrected, not weakened, to reflect this deliberate one-field exception, with the reasoning recorded in T64-implementation.md section 5.
summary_markdown: See T64-implementation.md for the full shape argument (flag-and-reason vs re-deriving from STRICTEST_GATE), the HealthConfig/computeGate consumer enumeration and its method, the coverage-soft-floor determination, the verdict-unchanged proof, and per-regression evidence.

acceptance.criterion: AC4 (AFC-05): fixtures, a corrupted payload, a skipped required check and an incomplete area each produce the expected outcome; violations are not lost when another check is unavailable.
acceptance.evidence: Unchanged from T59 by design -- this task adds a reason, not new gate logic. config.test.ts's corrupted-payload fixtures (null, 42, unparseable JSON) still produce the strictest reachable HealthConfig, now additionally carrying configUnreadable:true and coverageSoftFloor:100. gate.test.ts's pre-existing 'missing required source is incomplete in strict and non-strict runs' and 'optional skipped source does not affect gate' tests pass unmodified, proving a skipped/incomplete area is still surfaced and a real violation is never dropped by the new reason line.

acceptance.criterion: An operator reading the gate result can tell that the configuration was unusable, from a constant, leak-safe reason; the verdicts themselves are unchanged from what the previous repair established.
acceptance.evidence: computeGate pushes a fixed, non-interpolated CONFIG_UNREADABLE_REASON string into GateResult.reasons whenever config.configUnreadable is true; that value reaches both keryx health run's persisted report (run.ts:152 -> HealthReport.gate) and keryx health gate's output (service.ts's gate(): reasons: latest.gate.reasons) through code read but not modified. gate.test.ts's new regression asserts identical status/coverage with and without the flag on identical other inputs, and asserts the reason string leaks no cwd path, no literal 'undefined', and no .metaproject/.json fragment.

changed_files.change: HealthConfig gains one additive optional field, configUnreadable?: boolean, documented as mirroring SecurityConfig.configUnreadable
the existing (T59) present-but-unusable branch now also sets configUnreadable:true and forces metrics.coverageSoftFloor to 100; one stale comment corrected to name the coverageSoftFloor exception

computeGate pushes a new module-local constant, CONFIG_UNREADABLE_REASON, onto reasons when config.configUnreadable is true -- unconditional on any other gate condition, never calling escalate, so status/coverage are unchanged

one existing assertion corrected (metrics/coverageSoftFloor split, justified in the implementation report section 5); one new test proving configUnreadable is set only for the unusable case, undefined for absent/well-formed
two new tests: the flag adds a reason without moving the verdict (same status/coverage, different reasons, leak-safety asserted), and the reason still appears on an otherwise-clean gate
